name: cx-rules-only~p1
task: Never pick up the box in the other room. Try not to drop the key while the door is still closed, and whenever you hold the key, try to have the door open then or open it later.

value.feedback: NO CHANGES NEEDED: The three clauses map one-to-one onto the task's three requirements. 'Never pick up the box in the other room' is a categorical never with no preference cue, so the hard Absence(target_picked_up) is right, and the machine sends target_picked_up to the rejecting well u1. 'Try not to drop the key while the door is still closed' carries the cue 'Try not to', making it soft; since key_lost is defined as the key dropped while door_open is false, the condition is baked into the event and the plain soft Absence(key_lost) is the correct template (there is no 'until' wording, so no Precedence is needed); the machine charges the -1 soft penalty and the episode goes on. 'Whenever you hold the key, try to have the door open then or open it later' is exactly the soft Response(has_door_key, door_open) with the condition first and the consequent at that step or later: the machine shows the promise pending in u2, fulfilled with +1 when the door opens, and still owed with a penalty if the episode ends before an opening, including after the key is dropped with the door closed. The 'whenever' event is only a condition, so no Existence is demanded; the rule-only warning is valid because the task contains no unconditionally hard-commanded goal; all identifiers are declared and every clause is satisfiable in this environment.
